extracted.intended_audience: readers, translators, distributors, and re-publishers of Project Gutenberg eBooks (and translators/authors of the eBook)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for translating/presenting a literary work (translator's fidelity and presentation choices) together with the Project Gutenberg formal license and redistribution rules that govern copying, modifying, formatting, and commercial use of the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator fidelity / no interpolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Translator claims: 'I have intermix'd nothing of my own in the Amours of Zeokinizul: But, like a faithful Translator, I have constantly kept close to Krinelbol's Manuscript.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate without diminishing, augmenting, or altering the original in any particular; preserve the facts as told in the original manuscript. Offer access to the original manuscript on demand to remove suspicion of interpolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of names and official titles in translation
rubrics_metrics.description: For reader convenience, the translator: 'have expressed the Names of Posts and Dignities in our Language, which in the Original were in Arabic, keeping to it in the Appellations of Persons and Nations, out of regard to historical Exactness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate official ranks/posts/dignities into equivalents in the target language for reader comprehension, but retain original-language forms for personal and nation names to preserve historical exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preface inclusion and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Preface is considered essential ('a Preface was no less essential to a Book, than an Exordium to a Sermon') but 'as few read the one... the shorter a Preface is the better it is liked.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a preface when required by publisher/bookseller expectations, but keep it concise; avoid adding unnecessary discourse or amplification that could mislead or be injurious.
